summary: Completed iteration 5 regression testing for the portfolio across the public URL. Production build, backend persistence checks, required routes, project index, Aari text removal, email/em-dash checks, photography modal, mobile navigation, console errors, and responsive overflow were verified.

integration_issues.issue: Direct navigation to /work/aari-label still renders the first project (Akirah Label) because CaseStudy falls back to projects[0] for unknown slugs. No Aari text is exposed, but the removed route is not rejected and an invalid URL shows misleading content.

action_items: Handle unknown /work/:slug routes explicitly (404/not-found or redirect) instead of rendering Akirah as a fallback, then retest the removed Aari URL.
critical_code_review_comments: CaseStudy's projects.find(...) || projects[0] fallback makes deleted or mistyped project URLs resolve to unrelated project content; use an explicit not-found state or route handling.
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_-prefixed status record through the existing persistence regression test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL tested at desktop 1920px and mobile 390px. Three required projects and all remaining routes pass; six photography modal behavior was spot-checked for open/close; mobile menu reaches About. Source scan found no Aari text, em dash, old email, or placeholder email. No auth flow or mocked API applies.
rca of the issue: CaseStudy uses const project = projects.find((item) => item.slug === slug) || projects[0], so removing Aari from portfolioData removes its visible content but does not remove the dynamic route's ability to accept the slug. The fallback then displays Akirah for /work/aari-label.
